items.name: Gujarati Surti Winter Undhiyu

ingredients.name: Yam, peeled and cut into chunks
Green plantain, peeled and cut into chunks
Green beans, cut into short lengths

steps: Rub the chopped fenugreek with ground peanut, coconut, coriander, and a spoonful of oil to make a loose green stuffing.
Pack some of the mixture into the eggplant quarters, then layer them with the yam, plantain, and beans in a broad heavy pot.
Pour the remaining seasoning and hot water over the vegetables, cover tightly, and cook slowly until every piece is tender without being stirred to a mash.
items.guidance: Slow cooking unites the many vegetables in this celebratory winter undhiyu Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: keep the nut and oil portions light and favor more beans than roots.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Gujarati Dudhi Chana Dal
steps: Simmer the soaked chana dal until its centers soften while the grains still keep their shape.
Add the bottle-gourd cubes, chopped tomatoes, and turmeric, then cook until the vegetable becomes translucent.
Bloom cumin in ghee, stir the tempering into the dal, and scatter chopped cilantro over the pot after seasoning.
items.guidance: Moist bottle gourd makes chana dal easier to enjoy as a complete Gujarati main Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Gujarati Sweet-Sour Toor Dal
steps: Cook the pigeon pea with turmeric until it becomes smooth enough to whisk into a flowing dal.
Simmer in the diluted tamarind and grated jaggery, tasting for a gentle balance rather than pronounced sweetness.
Crackle cumin, mustard, and fenugreek in ghee, pour the tempering into the pot, and let the dal settle covered.
items.guidance: Mild sweet and sour notes distinguish this fluid Gujarati dal Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: reduce the tamarind and emphasize cumin rather than chili. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Gujarati Cumin Yogurt Kadhi
steps: Whisk the sifted chickpea flour into the yogurt, then thin the mixture gradually with hot water until no lumps remain.
Cook the kadhi over moderate heat while stirring until it boils gently and loses the flour's raw aroma.
Sizzle cumin, fenugreek, and grated ginger in ghee, pour them into the pot, and finish with a restrained touch of jaggery and salt.
items.guidance: Careful whisking and simmering give this Gujarati kadhi a light, even body Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: take a small bowl and strengthen the ginger while reducing the sweetener.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Gujarati Eggplant Potato Shaak

ingredients.name: Potatoes, peeled and cut into small cubes

steps: Toast cumin in sesame oil, add the potato cubes, and turn them until their edges become lightly golden.
Fold in the eggplant with turmeric and coriander, splash the pan with hot water, and cover until both vegetables yield.
Remove the lid, dust with amchur and salt, and reduce any moisture until the shaak carries a clinging spice coat.
items.guidance: Soft eggplant and potato make this Gujarati shaak grounding and substantial Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: use less amchur and serve with cooling greens. Kapha: reduce the potato portion and use only enough oil to prevent sticking.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Gujarati Okra Peanut Shaak

ingredients.name: Okra, wiped dry and cut into rounds

steps: Spread the dry okra rounds in hot peanut oil and let their cut faces sear before turning them.
Sprinkle coriander and turmeric over the pan, then cook uncovered until the pieces stop drawing sticky threads.
Toss in the coarse peanut, sesame, amchur, and salt, and remove the shaak when the nut coating smells toasted.
items.guidance: A nutty dry coating gives this Gujarati okra shaak generous texture Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: reduce the amchur and favor coriander. Kapha: halve the peanut mixture and keep the oil modest.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Gujarati Cabbage Pea Sambharo

ingredients.name: Cabbage, cut into very fine ribbons

steps: Pop the mustard in sesame oil, then add turmeric and the slit chili without allowing either to darken.
Toss the fine cabbage ribbons and peas over brisk heat until they warm through but retain a gentle crunch.
Take the sambharo off the flame, season it, and distribute the lemon juice only after the pan stops sizzling.
items.guidance: Brief cooking preserves the fresh character of this Gujarati cabbage sambharo Vata: cook the cabbage a little longer and add a spoon of ghee. Pitta: omit the chili and reduce the lemon. Kapha: keep the quick, dry texture and use the mustard generously.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Gujarati Pumpkin Fenugreek Shaak

ingredients.name: Pumpkin, peeled and cut into cubes

steps: Warm cumin in sesame oil, then add the pumpkin cubes and turmeric while the seeds are still fragrant.
Scatter over the chopped fenugreek, pour in a small amount of hot water, and cover until the pumpkin is tender.
Uncover, add coriander and salt, and turn the pieces carefully as the remaining liquid evaporates.
items.guidance: Bitter fenugreek balances sweet pumpkin in this simple Gujarati shaak Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Gujarati Spinach Mung Shaak
steps: Simmer the soaked mung until the beans are tender yet mostly intact.
Cook the chopped tomatoes and ginger in a second pan until pulpy, then wilt the spinach into them.
Combine the greens with the mung, finish with cumin bloomed in ghee, and season after the textures have settled together.
items.guidance: Whole mung gives this spinach shaak enough substance for a light midday meal Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Gujarati Green Bean Sesame Shaak

ingredients.name: Green beans, cut into small diamonds

steps: Toast cumin in sesame oil, then add the bean diamonds and turmeric with a splash of hot water.
Cover the pan until the beans are tender, opening it once to turn the lower pieces upward.
Cook away the moisture before tossing through coriander, ground sesame, amchur, and salt.
items.guidance: Sesame gives these gently steamed green beans a savory Gujarati finish Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Gujarati Stuffed Bitter Gourd
steps: Scoop the coarse seeds from the gourds, salt the cavities lightly, and leave them while the filling is mixed.
Combine roasted chickpea flour, ground peanut, coriander, cumin, and amchur, then pack the crumbly mixture into each slit.
Arrange the stuffed gourds in warm sesame oil, add a splash of hot water, and cook covered before browning every side uncovered.
items.guidance: A roasted gram filling softens the assertive bitterness of this Gujarati main Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: use less amchur and pair the dish with a mild grain. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Gujarati Mung Brown Rice Khichdi
steps: Warm cumin in ghee, then coat the soaked rice and split mung with turmeric in the fragrant pot.
Add the carrot cubes and hot water, bring everything to a lively boil, and lower the heat beneath a tight lid.
Cook until the grains are very soft, stir the khichdi to an even consistency, and season before a short covered rest.
items.guidance: Extended cooking makes brown rice and mung soft enough for this comforting Gujarati khichdi Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Gujarati Tomato Besan Ribbons
steps: Beat the chickpea flour with part of the hot water and a spoonful of oil to form a thick, smooth batter.
Cook the chopped tomatoes with cumin, turmeric, and coriander until they collapse into a loose sauce.
Drizzle the batter into the simmering gravy in thin ribbons, cook them through without vigorous stirring, and finish with cilantro and salt.
items.guidance: Tender chickpea ribbons turn a bright tomato gravy into a complete Gujarati dish Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: replace part of the tomato with bottle gourd and omit chili. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Rajasthani Ajwain Gatte Curry
steps: Knead the chickpea flour with crushed ajwain, part of the ghee, salt, and enough warm water to make a firm dough.
Roll the dough into narrow ropes, poach them until set, and slice the cooled ropes into bite-size coins.
Whisk yogurt into a coriander-and-turmeric gravy, simmer it steadily, then add the coins and remaining ghee until they absorb the sauce.
items.guidance: Poached chickpea dumplings make this Rajasthani yogurt curry dense and warming Vata: simmer the dumplings until very tender and serve with soft rice. Pitta: use mild spices and fresh, gently sour yogurt. Kapha: choose a small portion and reduce the ghee.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Rajasthani Five-Lentil Panchmel
steps: Soak the slower lentils, rinse all five together, and simmer them until every variety is completely tender.
Whisk the pot just enough to blend the red lentils into the broth while leaving some grains visible.
Bloom cumin and asafoetida in ghee, pour the tempering over the panchmel, and season after a final gentle boil.
items.guidance: Thorough soaking and cooking are essential in this robust five-lentil dal Vata: eat a modest bowl with extra ghee and soft rice. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Rajasthani Bajra Mung Khichdi
steps: Toast cumin and grated ginger in ghee, then stir the cracked millet and split mung through the aromatic fat.
Add turmeric and hot water, bring the pot to a boil, and cook slowly until the grains lose their separate outlines.
Beat the khichdi to a soft texture, add salt, and let it rest covered so the millet finishes swelling.
items.guidance: Long cooking turns warming pearl millet into a soft Rajasthani khichdi Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: serve a smaller bowl and use less ghee with more ginger.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Rajasthani Jaisalmer Chana Yogurt Curry
steps: Simmer the soaked chickpeas until creamy inside, reserving some of their cooking broth.
Whisk the yogurt with sifted chickpea flour, coriander, and turmeric, then cook the mixture steadily until it thickens.
Fold in the tender chickpeas, loosen with reserved broth, and finish the curry with cumin crackled in ghee.
items.guidance: Chickpeas and yogurt make this Jaisalmer-style curry especially substantial Vata: use very soft chickpeas and a small serving with warm rice. Pitta: keep the yogurt mild and omit hot chili. Kapha: reduce the gravy and ghee and emphasize cumin.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Rajasthani Potato Onion Saag

ingredients.name: Potatoes, peeled and cut into wedges

steps: Heat the mustard oil until shimmering, lower the heat, and soften the sliced onions with cumin.
Add the potato wedges, turmeric, and coriander, turning them until the spice mixture coats every surface.
Splash in hot water, cover until the potatoes yield, then uncover and finish with amchur and salt.
items.guidance: Onion and mustard oil give this dry Rajasthani potato dish a warming edge Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: use ghee instead of mustard oil and reduce the amchur. Kapha: keep the potato portion modest and cook with minimal oil.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Rajasthani Pumpkin Amchur Sabzi

ingredients.name: Pumpkin, peeled and cut into chunks

steps: Warm cumin and crushed fennel in mustard oil until the seeds release their aroma.
Add the pumpkin chunks with turmeric, turn them through the spices, and steam them under a lid with a little hot water.
Uncover while the pieces still hold shape, sprinkle in amchur and salt, and reduce the pan juices to a glaze.
items.guidance: Fennel and amchur sharpen the natural sweetness of this Rajasthani pumpkin sabzi Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: use less amchur and replace mustard oil with ghee. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Rajasthani Bottle Gourd Chana

ingredients.name: Bottle gourd, peeled and cut into chunks

steps: Cook the soaked chickpeas until fully tender, keeping enough broth to moisten the finished curry.
Soften cumin and chopped tomatoes in ghee, then add the bottle-gourd chunks and ground coriander.
Pour in the chickpeas and reserved broth, simmer until the gourd becomes translucent, and season once the gravy thickens.
items.guidance: Bottle gourd adds moisture to an otherwise dense chickpea curry Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Rajasthani Bajra Methi Pilaf

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger, cut into thin slivers

steps: Sauté the chopped fenugreek and ginger slivers in ghee until the leaves darken slightly.
Stir in the soaked millet and peas, coating the grains with the green mixture and toasted cumin.
Add hot water, cover, and cook until the millet is tender; rest the pilaf before loosening it with a fork.
items.guidance: Fenugreek brings balance to the warming density of pearl millet in this pilaf Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Rajasthani Besan Dumpling Pulao
steps: Mix the chickpea flour with crushed ajwain, salt, part of the ghee, and enough warm water to form a firm dough.
Shape tiny dumplings, poach them until set, and drain them while the rice and peas begin cooking with cumin.
Nestle the dumplings into the nearly tender rice, add the remaining ghee, and steam the pulao until the grains are dry and separate.
items.guidance: Small chickpea dumplings make this Rajasthani pulao filling without cheese Vata: make the dumplings small and tender and serve with a moist vegetable. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: reduce the ghee and keep the serving moderate.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Rajasthani Spinach Chickpea Curry
steps: Cook the soaked chickpeas until soft enough to crush between two fingers, then reserve their broth.
Collapse the chopped tomatoes in ghee with cumin and pepper before wilting in the spinach.
Add the chickpeas and enough reserved broth for a thick curry, simmer the flavors together, and season at the end.
items.guidance: Spinach lightens a hearty chickpea curry while pepper keeps it warming Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Rajasthani Fenugreek Lentil Stew
steps: Simmer the brown lentils with turmeric until tender, adding the carrot cubes once the broth begins to darken.
Fold the chopped fenugreek into the pot and cook until its raw bitterness becomes pleasantly mellow.
Pour over cumin warmed in ghee, adjust the stew to a spoonable consistency, and season before resting it.
items.guidance: Fenugreek and lentils make a warming, practical desert-region stew Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Rajasthani Carrot Pea Sabzi

ingredients.name: Carrots, peeled and cut into small cubes

steps: Bloom cumin and crushed fennel in ghee, then tumble in the carrot cubes with turmeric.
Add a little hot water, cover until the carrots begin to soften, and stir in the peas for the last few minutes.
Remove the lid, let the pan dry, and finish the sabzi with amchur and salt.
items.guidance: Sweet carrots and peas respond well to the dry warmth of cumin and fennel Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Punjabi Slow-Cooked Rajma

ingredients.name: Kidney beans, soaked overnight and drained

steps: Simmer the soaked kidney beans until their skins are supple and their centers mash without resistance.
Brown the diced onions gently in ghee, add cumin, ginger, coriander, and chopped tomatoes, and cook the masala until cohesive.
Fold in the beans with their broth, crush a few against the pot, and simmer slowly until the rajma becomes velvety.
items.guidance: Thorough soaking and long simmering are central to this rich Punjabi rajma Vata: take a small portion with ghee and soft white rice. Pitta: keep the tomato and ginger modest. Kapha: reduce ghee and accompany with bitter greens.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Punjabi Amritsari Fennel Chole
steps: Cook the soaked chickpeas until creamy within, reserving the dark cooking liquid.
Soften the sliced onions in ghee, toast cumin and fennel among them, and reduce the chopped tomatoes to a thick base.
Add the chickpeas and enough reserved broth to simmer, then finish the chole with amchur and salt once the gravy clings.
items.guidance: Fennel softens the sharp edge of this robust Punjabi chickpea curry Vata: use very tender chickpeas and a small serving. Pitta: reduce tomato and amchur. Kapha: keep the ghee low and emphasize the warming spices.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Punjabi Urad Rajma Makhani

ingredients.name: Black gram, whole and soaked overnight
Kidney beans, soaked overnight and drained

steps: Cook the soaked black gram and kidney beans until the skins split and the liquid turns naturally creamy.
Warm cumin and grated ginger in ghee, reduce the tomato puree until its raw scent disappears, and stir it into the beans.
Simmer the dal slowly while crushing some grains, then take it off direct heat before swirling in the cream and salt.
items.guidance: Long cooking gives this modern restaurant-style dal its characteristic richness Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: choose a very small bowl and omit the cream. Compliant variant: omit both cream and tomato, enrich the black gram with a little ghee, and brighten it with coriander.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Punjabi Fennel Palak Paneer

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger, cut into thin slivers

steps: Wilt the chopped spinach with a splash of hot water, cool it briefly, and blend only until the leaves form a textured puree.
Warm cumin, fennel, and ginger slivers in ghee, then add the paneer cubes and turn them gently.
Pour the green puree around the paneer, simmer without overcooking the color, and season before serving.
items.guidance: Fennel and spinach keep this tomato-free paneer preparation mild Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use less paneer and fill the plate with extra spinach.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Punjabi Pea Paneer Fennel Gravy
steps: Soften the diced fennel bulb in ghee until translucent, then blend half of it with the soaked cashews and hot water.
Return the pale sauce to the pan, season it with ground fennel and turmeric, and simmer until smooth.
Add the peas and paneer cubes, warm them gently without vigorous stirring, and adjust the gravy before serving.
items.guidance: A tomato-free fennel and cashew gravy supports peas and paneer without sharp sourness Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: reduce paneer and cashew and use more peas.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Punjabi Baked Pakora Kadhi
steps: Mix the sliced onions with most of the chickpea flour, crushed ajwain, salt, and enough warm water to hold rough mounds together.
Brush the mounds with a little ghee and bake them until set and golden at their craggy edges.
Simmer the yogurt with the remaining flour and turmeric, temper it with cumin in ghee, and soak the baked pakoras in the hot kadhi.
items.guidance: Baking keeps the pakoras lighter while preserving the comforting character of Punjabi kadhi Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: serve fewer pakoras and make the kadhi thin and well spiced.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Punjabi Mustard Spinach Saag
steps: Simmer the mustard greens until nearly tender, then add the spinach and cook until both collapse completely.
Work the fine cornmeal into the pot a little at a time and mash the greens to a coarse, thick saag.
Brown the sliced garlic and grated ginger in ghee, stir the tempering into the greens, and season after a final simmer.
items.guidance: Mustard greens and spinach create a warming winter saag with a rustic texture Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Punjabi Cumin Aloo Gobi

ingredients.name: Potatoes, peeled and cut into cubes

steps: Toast cumin in ghee, add the potato cubes, and turn them until their surfaces begin to color.
Fold in the cauliflower florets with turmeric and coriander, splash in hot water, and cover until both vegetables are tender.
Uncover to dry the pan, season the aloo gobi, and scatter chopped cilantro over it just before serving.
items.guidance: Cumin and thorough cooking help balance the dry qualities of cauliflower and potato Vata: add a little extra ghee and cook the florets very tender. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: reduce the potato portion and keep the fat light.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Punjabi Smoky Eggplant Bharta
steps: Cool the roasted eggplant, peel away the charred skin, and mash the smoky flesh with a fork.
Soften the diced onions and cumin in ghee, add the chopped tomatoes, and cook them into a concentrated masala.
Stir in the mashed eggplant and peas, cook until the bharta is cohesive, and finish with salt and chopped cilantro.
items.guidance: Roasting concentrates eggplant for a smoky Punjabi bharta Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: use fewer tomatoes and avoid additional chili. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Punjabi Bottle Gourd Besan Kofta

ingredients.name: Bottle gourd, peeled and grated coarse

steps: Squeeze the grated gourd lightly, mix it with chickpea flour and salt, and shape the moist mixture into small balls.
Brush the balls with part of the ghee and bake them until their surfaces set and turn golden.
Reduce the tomato puree with cumin and coriander, loosen the gravy with hot water, and warm the baked koftas in it just before serving.
items.guidance: Baked bottle-gourd koftas keep this Punjabi gravy lighter than a fried version Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: replace half the tomato with a pureed fennel bulb. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Punjabi Methi Matar Fennel
steps: Soften the diced fennel bulb in ghee, then blend half with the soaked cashews and hot water.
Cook the chopped fenugreek in the same pan until its raw bitterness mellows, and add the peas.
Pour in the pale fennel sauce, simmer until it coats the vegetables, and season without burying the fresh green flavor.
items.guidance: A mild fennel sauce balances bitter fenugreek and sweet peas Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Punjabi Chana Palak
steps: Cook the soaked chickpeas until fully tender and reserve enough broth to moisten the curry.
Warm cumin and grated ginger in ghee, reduce the chopped tomatoes, and wilt the spinach into the masala.
Add the chickpeas and reserved broth, simmer until the greens cling to the beans, and season at the end.
items.guidance: Spinach gives hearty chickpeas a greener, lighter Punjabi profile Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: use fewer tomatoes and keep the ginger modest. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Punjabi Cumin Pea Brown Rice
steps: Warm cumin and the bay leaf in ghee until the seeds deepen a shade and smell nutty.
Add the soaked brown rice, turn the grains through the fragrant fat, and pour in hot water.
Cover and cook gently, scatter in the peas near the end, and rest the rice before removing the leaf and fluffing.
items.guidance: Extended cooking and ghee soften the dry character of brown rice in this cumin pilaf Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Bengali Mung Shukto

ingredients.name: Bitter gourd, sliced into thin half-moons
Green plantain, peeled and cut into batons
Potatoes, peeled and cut into batons
Mustard seeds, ground to a paste

steps: Brown the bitter-gourd slices in a little ghee and lift them out before they become brittle.
Add the plantain and potato batons to the pot, then the eggplant, and simmer with hot water until each is tender.
Stir in the ground mung, mustard, and poppy paste, return the bitter gourd, and cook the shukto to a pale, lightly bitter gravy.
items.guidance: Bitter vegetables and a pale seed gravy define this Bengali shukto Vata: eat a modest portion with warm rice and enough ghee. Pitta: keep mustard gentle and do not add chili. Kapha: favor the bitter vegetables and reduce potato.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Bengali Coconut Cholar Dal

ingredients.name: Fresh coconut, cut into tiny chips

steps: Cook the soaked chana dal until tender while keeping the grains intact enough to see.
Brown the coconut chips in ghee, add cumin, the bay leaf, and cracked cinnamon, and let the spices perfume the fat.
Pour the tempering into the dal, add a restrained touch of jaggery and salt, and simmer until the broth lightly coats the lentils.
items.guidance: Coconut chips and whole spices give this Bengali cholar dal a festive character Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: reduce coconut and jaggery and choose a smaller portion.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Bengali Roasted Mung Dal
steps: Dry-roast the split mung over moderate heat until the grains smell nutty but remain golden rather than brown.
Rinse the warm grains, simmer them with turmeric, and add the tomato wedges once the dal is nearly tender.
Bloom cumin and the bay leaf in ghee, stir the tempering into the pot, and season without over-mashing the lentils.
items.guidance: Dry roasting gives Bengali mung dal a distinctive nutty aroma Vata: add enough ghee and cook the roasted grains very soft. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Bengali Potato Poppy Seed Curry

ingredients.name: Potatoes, peeled and cut into slim wedges

steps: Warm the mustard oil, pop the seeds, and add the potato wedges with the slit chili.
Turn the potatoes until their edges color, then add hot water and cover until they are nearly tender.
Stir in the smooth poppy paste, simmer uncovered until it clings to the wedges, and season the curry.
items.guidance: A creamy poppy coating defines this Bengali potato preparation Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: omit the chili and replace mustard oil with ghee. Kapha: keep the potato and seed portions modest.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Bengali Eggplant Poppy Seed Curry
steps: Sear the eggplant wedges in mustard oil until their cut sides bronze and the skins stay taut.
Sprinkle over turmeric, add hot water, and cover until the flesh becomes silky without collapsing.
Ease the ground poppy paste around the wedges, simmer until thick, and season while shaking the pan instead of stirring hard.
items.guidance: Poppy paste gives tender eggplant a mild, velvety Bengali sauce Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: use ghee in place of mustard oil and keep the seasoning mild. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Bengali Pumpkin Bean Chorchori

ingredients.name: Pumpkin, peeled and cut into slim pieces
Green beans, cut into short lengths
Potatoes, peeled and cut into slim pieces

steps: Pop mustard in the warm oil, add turmeric, and lay the potato pieces in the pan first.
Add the beans and pumpkin in stages, sprinkle with hot water, and cover so the vegetables steam in their mingled juices.
Uncover and turn the mixture carefully until the pumpkin lightly coats the other pieces, then season the chorchori.
items.guidance: Pumpkin binds several vegetables into a soft-edged Bengali chorchori Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Bengali Cabbage Chickpea Ghonto

ingredients.name: Potatoes, peeled and cut into small cubes

steps: Cook the soaked chickpeas until tender and drain them, keeping a cup of their broth nearby.
Warm cumin and the bay leaf in ghee, add the potato cubes with turmeric, and brown their edges lightly.
Heap in the shredded cabbage and chickpeas, cover until soft, then uncover and stir until the ghonto becomes almost dry.
items.guidance: Chickpeas turn slow-cooked cabbage into a complete Bengali ghonto Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Bengali Spinach Chana Dal
steps: Simmer the soaked chana dal with turmeric until tender while preserving some shape in each grain.
Fold in the chopped spinach and cook uncovered until the greens are soft and the broth thickens again.
Bloom cumin and crushed fennel in ghee, pour the tempering through the dal, and season before serving.
items.guidance: Fennel keeps this spinach and chana dal preparation aromatic but gentle Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Bengali Baked Dhokar Dalna

ingredients.name: Potatoes, peeled and cut into cubes

steps: Grind the soaked chana dal to a thick paste, cook it in part of the ghee until it leaves the pan, and spread it in a shallow tray.
Cut the cooled slab into diamonds, brush them lightly with ghee, and bake until the edges become firm.
Simmer potato cubes in a cumin, ginger, and tomato gravy, then add the baked lentil cakes just long enough to absorb some sauce.
items.guidance: Baking gives these Bengali lentil cakes structure without deep frying Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: replace part of the tomato with pumpkin and keep ginger modest. Kapha: serve fewer cakes and reduce the ghee.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Bengali Mustard Eggplant
steps: Brown the eggplant wedges in mustard oil and turn them carefully so their skins remain attached.
Mix the ground mustard and poppy with hot water, turmeric, and salt, then pour the pale sauce around the vegetables.
Add the slit chili, cover until the flesh is tender, and uncover briefly to mellow the mustard without boiling it hard.
items.guidance: Mustard gives this Bengali eggplant curry a penetrating, pungent character Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: omit the chili, use less mustard, and dilute the sauce generously. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Odia Cumin Vegetable Santula

ingredients.name: Bottle gourd, peeled and cut into chunks
Pumpkin, peeled and cut into chunks

steps: Layer the bottle gourd and beans beneath the quicker-softening pumpkin and eggplant in a wide pot.
Add hot water and salt, cover, and let the vegetables steam gently until each is tender but recognizable.
Warm cumin and crushed garlic in ghee, fold the tempering through the santula, and serve it with its light broth.
items.guidance: Gentle steaming keeps this mixed-vegetable Odia santula light and moist Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Odia Pumpkin Vegetable Dalma

ingredients.name: Pumpkin, peeled and cut into chunks
Green plantain, peeled and cut into chunks

steps: Cook the pigeon pea until halfway tender, then add the firm plantain before the pumpkin and eggplant.
Simmer until the dal becomes creamy and the vegetables soften without dissolving completely.
Crush the toasted cumin and fennel, stir them into the dalma with warm ghee, and season after the pot rests.
items.guidance: Vegetables cook directly with pigeon pea in this nourishing Odia dalma Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
